claims.text: The initial NbMoTaW alloy is equiatomic and single-phase BCC.
NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical strength at temperatures up to 1600 °C.
The irradiation resistance of NbMoTaW has only been inferred computationally.
Deep cryogenic treatment will induce microstructural modifications in NbMoTaW.
Deep cryogenic treatment will improve the room-temperature ductility of NbMoTaW.
Deep cryogenic treatment will improve the irradiation tolerance of NbMoTaW.
Deep cryogenic treatment will preserve the high-temperature mechanical strength of NbMoTaW up to 1600 °C.
Deep cryogenic treatment may produce nanoscale precipitates, subgrain boundaries, or localized phase transitions in NbMoTaW.
The DCT-induced microstructural features will increase the availability of active slip systems.
The DCT-induced microstructural features will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment will relieve residual stresses in NbMoTaW.
Deep cryogenic treatment will induce subtle phase transformations or solute redistribution in NbMoTaW.
Additional slip systems generated by these changes will enhance room-temperature ductility.
The new microstructural features will trap and annihilate irradiation-induced defects.
DCT-treated NbMoTaW will exhibit lower post-irradiation defect density than untreated NbMoTaW.
DCT-treated NbMoTaW will show less irradiation-induced amorphization, surface blistering, and precipitation than untreated NbMoTaW.
The proposed benefit will extend from room temperature to 1600 °C under helium-ion implantation conditions associated with blistering and precipitation.
In a different BCC Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr-based alloy, DCT induced a phase transition and increased tensile strength and elongation.

contradictions.description: The proposal invokes DCT-induced precipitates or localized phase transformations while also seeking to preserve single-phase BCC structural stability and reduce irradiation-enhanced precipitation; it does not distinguish beneficial treatment-induced secondary features from destabilizing phases or irradiation-induced precipitates.
